authorization: User requested planning an alternative signal-capture requirement using a subagent. This file authorizes no governed changes or case runs.
recommended_decision: Develop a separately versioned CAP-OWNED-CONTAINMENT-CLEANUP/1 feasibility candidate for trusted, direct-launch cached/synthetic workloads. Keep CAP-SIGNAL-CAPTURE false and frozen v2.7 untouched. Do not claim arbitrary same-account process containment.

prior_design.finding: Job Object design A was correctly rejected as an exhaustive per-PID/parent-at-signal evidence mechanism. Its containment-only status is compatible with this proposed different requirement, not a reversal of that rejection.
prior_design.existing_backend: tools/workflow/processes.py uses taskkill /PID /T /F on Windows, then waits only for the root; observer records explicitly deny exhaustive_signal_capture. Root exit alone does not meet this candidate requirement.

contract.normative_proposal: Before executing any owned workload instruction, establish and verify an owned process boundary. Record each launch admission, closure of admission, every boundary termination request and native return/error, and the observed cleanup result. CLEAN requires a successful authoritative query showing zero active boundary processes after admission is closed, with no observed escape, evidence gap, or supervisor crash. Unknown evidence never becomes zero.
contract.not_equivalent_to: CAP-SIGNAL-CAPTURE: no enumeration of actual termination targets, exact parent-at-signal relationships, proof of every signal sent, or assertion that decoys received zero signals.

statuses.CLEAN: Boundary and launch scope verified; no integrity/observation gap; admission permanently closed; successful zero-active query before deadline; required stop request succeeded when requested.
statuses.FAILED: Observed escape, unauthorized launch/termination scope, positive active count at deadline, failed required stop API, or configured containment violation. Independent later cleanup does not erase failure.
statuses.UNKNOWN: Missing/failed query, lost identity or journal, supervisor crash, unproved broker or alternate-parent coverage, or incomplete crash recovery. Best-effort cleanup still runs.
statuses.REFUSED_BEFORE_EXECUTION: Containment prerequisites or supported launch class absent; no workload instruction admitted. Distinct from CLEAN and from successful case execution.

contract.zero_launch_branch: Emit observed admission count zero, a configured empty boundary and successful zero query; never synthesize an empty signal list as exhaustive evidence.
contract.timeout_policy: Initial canary proposal: workload deadline 5 seconds, cleanup deadline 10 seconds, serialized cases. Record actual values. Positive count at deadline FAILED; unavailable count UNKNOWN. These values are not frozen benchmark budgets.
contract.future_admission: After terminal zero query, no trusted launcher may add processes. Close or revoke assign handles before finalization; retain only query access until evidence is persisted. Restart uses a new boundary and attempt ID.

mechanism.candidate: Windows Job Object owned by a supervisor outside the workload job; KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE set, both breakaway flags unset, no inherited workload job handles, controlled handle duplication only.
mechanism.launch: Prefer CreateProcess with STARTUPINFOEX PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST and CREATE_SUSPENDED, verify membership before ResumeThread. This avoids the unassigned suspended-process crash window. Plain suspended-create then AssignProcessToJobObject is fallback only with a separately proved pre-assignment cleanup guardian; otherwise reject it.
mechanism.termination: Close admission first; call TerminateJobObject using the retained owned handle; persist request and return independently; query JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation until ActiveProcesses is zero or deadline expires. API return or root exit alone is insufficient.
mechanism.observations: Completion-port events and PID snapshots may assist diagnostics, never establish completeness or substitute for successful accounting query. ActiveProcesses is an instantaneous job count, not an assertion about outside brokers. Do not use generic job-handle signaled state as a universal zero-process condition.
mechanism.crash: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE is best-effort crash cleanup conditioned on last-handle closure. A surviving monitor holding a duplicate prevents that trigger; it must actively terminate on supervisor death. Every supervisor crash attempt remains UNKNOWN even if independent cleanup canary confirms exit. No automatic resumption of an unknown attempt.
mechanism.integration: Opt-in backend selection at Processes launch/stop boundaries, leaving adapter-off behavior intact; all observation exceptions must preserve cleanup and original process failure. No implementation in this planning task.

unsupported: alternate-parent process attributes outside owned job
threat_boundary.escape_rule: An observed outside launch is FAILED. An allowed binary capable of unreviewed broker/alternate-parent launch is UNKNOWN or refused before execution. Ordinary Job Objects do not prove no such launches occurred; an allowlisted cached/synthetic profile is an explicit trust assumption, not OS enforcement.
threat_boundary.decoy_rule: Use only a harness-owned harmless decoy outside the boundary with retained process identity. Verify decoy remains alive and responsive; this proves survival, not absence of every signal or effect. Never target unrelated processes.

canaries.scenario: Refuse invalid job setup, membership, flags or resume failure
canaries.acceptance: No workload marker before verified admission; every created owned process cleaned; refusal is not CLEAN execution.
Successful zero query after admission closed; no fabricated termination request.
Owned-job termination request/result and observed zero by deadline; external decoy responsive.
All fixtures verified members before release barrier; termination and authoritative zero; cancellation reason retained.

canaries.scenario: Root exits before child/grandchild; rapid direct child churn
canaries.acceptance: Root exit cannot finalize CLEAN while job count positive; cleanup of remaining members; no reliance on notification completeness.

canaries.scenario: Breakaway request and nested child job
canaries.acceptance: Observed membership remains in owned ancestor or creation denied. Any outside process FAILED. Record host parent-job constraints; unsupported nesting refused.

canaries.scenario: Owned external broker fixture and alternate-parent creation
canaries.acceptance: Do not enable real WMI/services. Owned broker fixture demonstrates outside creation is refused/detected as FAILED or UNKNOWN, never CLEAN. Candidate cannot graduate to arbitrary broker coverage.

canaries.scenario: Workload restarts itself within direct child chain
canaries.acceptance: Replacement stays owned; root PID change does not bypass cleanup; terminate by job identity.

canaries.scenario: Supervisor crash at pre-create, created-before-resume, running, stop-request, pre-zero-journal boundaries
canaries.acceptance: Independently retained owned identities show cleanup within deadline or report failure; every crashed attempt UNKNOWN. Explicitly test leaked job handle delaying KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.

canaries.scenario: Query failure, observer exception, lost completion message, journal failure
canaries.acceptance: Cleanup still attempted; missing authoritative evidence UNKNOWN. Missing optional completion messages alone do not invalidate successful query with intact mandatory journal.

canaries.scenario: Stop API failure and active count deadline exceeded
canaries.acceptance: FAILED regardless of root exit or later fallback cleanup; error and fallback provenance retained.
No blind rerun; investigate retained identity and owned cleanup evidence. New attempt ID and job only after prior outcome disposition recorded.

stages.work: Freeze candidate wording and supported trust profile; enumerate all launch pathways and host parent-job constraints.
stages.gate: Independent reviewer accepts semantic difference and threat boundary; original pins retained.

stages.work: Implement isolated small native-API canary only, with independent retained-handle cleanup owner and bounded deadlines.
stages.gate: Already authorized by the original work order: bounded owned synthetic feasibility canaries with explicit scope and cleanup. No additional HITL approval. Current task implements isolated canary only; technical API feasibility and retained-identity cleanup are gates.

stages.work: Run N0-N11 sequentially, recording native returns, memberships, observations, stderr and owned cleanup.
stages.gate: No escaped/unknown case labeled CLEAN; mandatory success cases meet zero-count deadline; limits documented.

stages.work: Review optional Processes backend integration and meaningful adapter-off regressions.
stages.gate: Canaries pass supported scope; independent review; observation failure cannot block cleanup or mask failure.

stages.work: Prepare separately named candidate caseset, evidence contract, predicates, requirements and negative probes; preserve originals.
stages.gate: Before proposing a governed change, verify current explicit authority and prepare a concrete independently reviewed successor. Existing work order prohibits frozen policy/scorer/ledger changes. No blanket 66-case human judgment gate; technical review is not HITL.

stages.work: Run separately identified candidate baseline/candidate pairs only after other capability requirements are implemented.
stages.gate: 66-case/33-pair coverage retained; no claimed frozen-v2.7 GS1 equivalence; unsupported and UNKNOWN denominators reported.

migration.all_66: All frozen cases require CAP-SIGNAL-CAPTURE and V26-PROCESS-OWNERSHIP. Candidate package must replace these explicitly with boundary-admission/scope/cleanup predicates, never alias capability names.
migration.V25_EVIDENCE: Review run_evidence/2 nested signal/process record requirements for all cases. Retain process receipts, resource accounting, chronology, parent-at-launch and all unrelated assertions; introduce new containment evidence schema instead of filling signalled_pids with synthetic values.
migration.special_E12_P2: Both INJ and CTL C1 require redesign from actual signal ancestry to owned-boundary stop scope. Preserve C2 decoy survival. C3 zero signals cannot be inferred; retain unsupported or explicitly replace with decoy liveness/no observed termination under a new owner-approved predicate. INJ C5 plot-onset signal requirement must become evidenced plot process membership, stop trigger and cleanup outcome while retaining no MAP_CREATED/RELEASED. This changes what is proved.
migration.other_requirements: Keep every non-signal capability and assertion; changing signal requirement alone does not make any case executable. Preserve execution_mode, stimuli, budgets, pairs, scientific restrictions, authentication and oracle governance.
migration.comparison: Candidate results must display their distinct contract/caseset/scorer hashes and never be counted as frozen v2.7 passes. Human owner must decide acceptable loss of signal specificity before any ratification.

primary_sources.supports: Direct CreateProcess descendants normally join; WMI launch exception; breakaway and kill-on-last-close semantics; completion delivery not generally guaranteed.
Termination targets current job and nested child jobs; nonzero native success and error reporting.
ActiveProcesses represents currently associated processes; use observed accounting rather than invented target lists.
Assignment constraints, nested-job behavior and failure reporting must be checked.
JOB_LIST assigns supplied job handles at creation; alternate-parent attribute can alter inherited job; Windows 10+ job-list support.

ratification_routing.status: ANALYTICAL ROUTING MAP; NOT A RATIFICATION LEDGER
ratification_routing.interpretation: Separate technical realizability and defects from shared policy premises and formal authority. No blanket 66-case human judgment prerequisite. This proposed loss of exact signal semantics is one shared contract decision plus E12 measurement consequences; technical canaries and implementation review can proceed independently. Analytical recommendations are not ledger authorization.
